_meta.indication: Treatment of schizophrenia in adults, and bipolar I disorder in adults (acute treatment of manic or mixed episodes as monotherapy and as adjunct to lithium or valproate; maintenance monotherapy treatment)
_meta.receipt_date: November 15, 2019 (original submission); resubmission/complete response received December 1, 2020

pivotal_trials.design: 4-week, multinational, randomized (1:1:1), double-blind, olanzapine- and placebo-controlled antipsychotic efficacy study in acute exacerbation of schizophrenia
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with acute exacerbation of schizophrenia
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in PANSS total score at Week 4
pivotal_trials.n: 403 randomized (ALKS 3831 132, olanzapine 132, placebo 133 in the PANSS analysis)
pivotal_trials.result: PANSS LS mean difference from placebo -6.4 (SE 1.8); 95% CI -10.0, -2.8; p<0.001, favoring ALKS 3831 (olanzapine -5.3; 95% CI -8.9, -1.7; p=0.004)

pivotal_trials.design: 24-week, randomized (1:1), double-blind, olanzapine-controlled weight mitigation study
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary: percent change in body weight from baseline to Week 24, and proportion of subjects with ≥10% weight gain from baseline to Week 24
pivotal_trials.result: Mean percent weight change lower with ALKS 3831: treatment difference -2.38% (95% CI -3.88%, -0.88%; p=0.003). ≥10% weight gain: 17.8% ALKS 3831 vs 29.8% olanzapine; odds ratio 0.50 (95% CI 0.31, 0.80; p=0.003)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions in schizophrenia (≥5% and ≥twice placebo): weight increased (19% vs 3% placebo), somnolence (9% vs 2%), dry mouth (7% vs 1%), headache (6% vs 3%). In the 24-week olanzapine-controlled trial: weight increased (25%), somnolence (21%), dry mouth (13%). Boxed warning for increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis.
target_moa: Fixed-dose combination of olanzapine (atypical antipsychotic; efficacy proposed via dopamine and serotonin type 2 (5HT2) antagonism) and samidorphan, an opioid receptor antagonist that acts primarily as a mu-opioid antagonist and is intended to mitigate olanzapine-associated weight gain
modality: small molecule (fixed-dose oral combination of olanzapine and samidorphan L-malate)

boxed_warning.content: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis; LYBALVI is not approved for the treatment of patients with dementia-related psychosis

rems.type: The Agency decided a REMS was not warranted, citing the precedent for acceptably safe use of other opioid receptor antagonists

advisory_committee.vote: Joint Psychopharmacologic Drugs and Drug Safety and Risk Management Advisory Committee (Oct 9, 2020): 16 Yes/1 No that samidorphan meaningfully mitigates weight gain; 13 Yes/3 No/1 Abstain on safety profile; 11 Yes/6 No that labeling was sufficient to mitigate opioid antagonist risks

basis.text: The application was reviewed under standard (not priority) review

summary.text: LYBALVI was approved as a 505(b)(2) NDA with a new molecular entity (samidorphan) under standard review. Efficacy relied on a PK bridge to olanzapine plus Study A305 demonstrating antipsychotic efficacy, and Study A303 demonstrating weight mitigation versus olanzapine. The original application received a Complete Response in the first review cycle due to manufacturing deficiencies; the resubmission was approved. A joint PDAC/DSaRM advisory committee was convened; no REMS was required.

citations.quote: Alkermes Inc Pharmaceuticals has resubmitted this 505(b)(2) NDA with new molecular entity (NME) for olanzapine/samidorphan for the treatment of schizophrenia and of bipolar I disorder, manic or mixed episodes and maintenance.

The efficacy of ALKS3831 for the proposed indication is established by an adequate PK bridge to listed drug olanzapine (NDA 020592), which allows to rely on a prior finding of efficacy of olanzapine for the proposed indication, and by Study 305, which provides evidence of effectiveness of ALKS 3831 on psychotic symptoms
In the first review cycle, the Agency identified drug product manufacturing facility deficiencies as well as drug product process deficiencies.
